ArmeniaAffordability Score: 7Tax Friendliness Score: 5Political Stability Score: 18Human Development Score: 14Government Effectiveness Score: 17Average Score: 12.2In the South Caucasus region, Armenia is an enticing option for immigrants. Its rich culture, historical significance, diverse landscapes, and warm welcome make it a unique destination. Armenia's 20% personal income tax, lower than many other countries, and its affordable living costs make it an appealing choice for those seeking economic opportunities in a culturally vibrant setting.15. VanuatuAffordability Score: 5Tax Friendliness Score: 1Political Stability Score: 10Human Development Score: 19Government Effectiveness Score: 20Average Score: 11Vanuatu offers a Citizenship by Investment program that allows individuals to obtain citizenship by making a non-refundable contribution of either $130,000 or $180,000 for a family of four. This contribution, often called a donation, is directed towards Vanuatu's local development fund. This donation's primary objective is to enhance the country's infrastructure, overall development, and economic progress within the region.14. RomaniaAffordability Score: 19Tax Friendliness Score: 3Political Stability Score: 12Human Development Score: 6Government Effectiveness Score: 14Average Score: 10.8Investors seeking Romanian citizenship must adhere to the standard naturalization process, which entails establishing their primary residence in Romania for at least eight years (or five years if married and cohabiting with a Romanian citizen). This duration can be reduced by half if the applicant invests at least EUR 1,000,000 in Romania, resulting in a four-year or two-and-a-half-year requirement for those married to a Romanian citizen. Furthermore, any year in which the applicant spends more than six months abroad is excluded from the calculation of the citizenship application period.13. St LuciaAffordability Score: 3Tax Friendliness Score: 9Political Stability Score: 9Human Development Score: 17Government Effectiveness Score: 13Average Score: 10.2Saint Lucia is one the cheapest Citizenship by Investment programs and offers multiple investment options. One is the National Economic Fund Contribution, with amounts ranging from US$100,000 to US$15,000, depending on family size. Another choice is real estate investment, requiring a minimum of US$200,000. The Government Bond Investment option mandates a US$300,000 investment for sole applicants, plus a US$50,000 administration fee. These options grant citizenship and support the country's economic growth.12. North MacedoniaAffordability Score: 9Tax Friendliness Score: 3Political Stability Score: 14Human Development Score: 13Government Effectiveness Score: 11Average Score: 10Under the Donation Route, individuals must contribute approximately $220,000 (€200,000) to a government-approved fund. Meanwhile, under the Investment Route, a direct investment of roughly $430,000 (€400,000) is necessary for the development of new facilities, excluding those in the hospitality sector. Additionally, a prerequisite of employing a minimum of ten individuals is mandated, thereby contributing to the creation of new job opportunities and the overall enhancement of the nation's economy.11. SeychellesAffordability Score: 20Tax Friendliness Score: 4Political Stability Score: 11Human Development Score: 11Government Effectiveness Score: 3Average Score: 9.8Seychelles offers citizenship to investors who have committed at least $1 million to a business in the country and have sustained their residency for a total of 11 years. Applicants must provide evidence of their investment in launching or expanding a business and meet other stipulated criteria to qualify. It's crucial to note that personal assets are not factored into the assessment. The eligibility conditions further mandate that applicants have maintained legal residence within Seychelles for an accumulated period of 11 years, without being absent for a continuous span of one year or more without the prior consent of the Minister of Internal Affairs.10. Cape VerdeAffordability Score: 8Tax Friendliness Score: 6Political Stability Score: 7Human Development Score: 18Government Effectiveness Score: 8Average Score: 9.4Cape Verde ranks 10th on our list of best Citizenship by Investment programs in 2023. Investors who make a substantial investment of $200,000 or more in the country can be granted citizenship. Cape Verde solicits investments in Energy, Tourism, and Infrastructure projects, with a particular emphasis on foreign investors who stimulate job creation and make substantial contributions to the nation's economic development.9. AustriaAffordability Score: 21Tax Friendliness Score: 13Political Stability Score: 6Human Development Score: 3Government Effectiveness Score: 2Average Score: 9The Austrian CBI program demands a significant financial commitment, typically from $2 to $10 million. However, this investment must be directed towards an active business that contributes to job creation or generates new export sales, with passive investments like government bonds, financial instruments, or real estate meeting the program's criteria. Moreover, participants in the program are required to uphold their investment for a minimum of 10 years. In addition to the financial commitment, applicants must demonstrate their ability to sustain themselves and their families in Austria.For investors that are looking to increase their exposure to the tax and financial management services markets, some stocks to consider include Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU), Automatic Data Processing (NASDAQ:ADP), and Broadridge Financial Solutions, Inc. (NYSE:BR).8. DominicaAffordability Score: 1Tax Friendliness Score: 10Political Stability Score: 1Human Development Score: 16Government Effectiveness Score: 13Average Score: 8.2Dominica continues to be recognized as one of the cheapest Citizenship by Investment programs globally. With its efficient and transparent process, Dominica's program offers individuals the opportunity to obtain citizenship through various investment options. These options include donating to the Economic Diversification Fund or investing in pre-approved real estate projects. With its reliable reputation and attractive incentives, Dominica remains a top choice for those seeking second citizenship through investment.7. MauritiusAffordability Score: 14Tax Friendliness Score: 4Political Stability Score: 8Human Development Score: 7Government Effectiveness Score: 5Average Score: 7.6With its stable political environment, strong economy, and high standard of living, Mauritius offers an attractive option for investors looking to obtain a residence, which can eventually lead to citizenship. The country's residence program provides a route to citizenship through various investment options, such as real estate, property & hotel development schemes, and approved businesses. Obtaining a passport through naturalization in Mauritius requires a minimum of five years, and citizenship can only be attained after securing a permanent residence permit, which is typically granted three years after obtaining the initial residence permit.6. MontenegroAffordability Score: 4Tax Friendliness Score: 2Political Stability Score: 16Human Development Score: 5Government Effectiveness Score: 10Average Score: 7.4Montenegro is one country offering a Citizenship by Investment program in 2023. This program allows individuals to obtain Montenegrin citizenship by investing significantly in the country. Montenegro is a country in Southeastern Europe known for its landscapes and rich cultural heritage. Montenegro CBI program provides various benefits to investors, including visa-free travel to over 120 countries, access to the European market, and a favorable tax regime.Click to continue reading and see the 5 Best Citizenship by Investment Programs in 2023.Suggested Articles:15 Cheapest CBI Programs in 202320 Countries that Have the Most Billionaires Per Capita20 Richest Countries in Africa Ranked by Net WorthDisclosure: None. 20 Best Citizenship by Investment Programs in 2023 is originally published on Insider Monkey.]

column4: Automatic Data Processing (NASDAQ:ADP) Has A Pretty Healthy Balance Sheet
column10: [The external fund manager backed by Berkshire Hathaway's Charlie Munger, Li Lu, makes no bones about it when he says 'The biggest investment risk is not the volatility of prices, but whether you will suffer a permanent loss of capital.' So it seems the smart money knows that debt - which is usually involved in bankruptcies - is a very important factor, when you assess how risky a company is. As with many other companies Automatic Data Processing, Inc. (NASDAQ:ADP) makes use of debt. But the more important question is: how much risk is that debt creating?When Is Debt Dangerous?Debt and other liabilities become risky for a business when it cannot easily fulfill those obligations, either with free cash flow or by raising capital at an attractive price. If things get really bad, the lenders can take control of the business. However, a more common (but still painful) scenario is that it has to raise new equity capital at a low price, thus permanently diluting shareholders. Of course, the upside of debt is that it often represents cheap capital, especially when it replaces dilution in a company with the ability to reinvest at high rates of return. When we think about a company's use of debt, we first look at cash and debt together. See our latest analysis for Automatic Data Processing What Is Automatic Data Processing's Debt?As you can see below, Automatic Data Processing had US$3.10b of debt, at June 2023, which is about the same as the year before. You can click the chart for greater detail. However, it also had US$2.10b in cash, and so its net debt is US$997.4m.debt-equity-history-analysisA Look At Automatic Data Processing's LiabilitiesThe latest balance sheet data shows that Automatic Data Processing had liabilities of US$42.8b due within a year, and liabilities of US$4.69b falling due after that. On the other hand, it had cash of US$2.10b and US$3.01b worth of receivables due within a year. So its liabilities total US$42.4b more than the combination of its cash and short-term receivables.Story continuesWhile this might seem like a lot, it is not so bad since Automatic Data Processing has a huge market capitalization of US$102.3b, and so it could probably strengthen its balance sheet by raising capital if it needed to. But we definitely want to keep our eyes open to indications that its debt is bringing too much risk. Carrying virtually no net debt, Automatic Data Processing has a very light debt load indeed.We use two main ratios to inform us about debt levels relative to earnings. The first is net debt divided by earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA), while the second is how many times its earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) covers its interest expense (or its interest cover, for short). This way, we consider both the absolute quantum of the debt, as well as the interest rates paid on it.Automatic Data Processing's net debt is only 0.20 times its EBITDA. And its EBIT covers its interest expense a whopping 43.9 times over. So you could argue it is no more threatened by its debt than an elephant is by a mouse. Also good is that Automatic Data Processing grew its EBIT at 19% over the last year, further increasing its ability to manage debt. The balance sheet is clearly the area to focus on when you are analysing debt. But ultimately the future profitability of the business will decide if Automatic Data Processing can strengthen its balance sheet over time. So if you want to see what the professionals think, you might find this free report on analyst profit forecasts to be interesting.But our final consideration is also important, because a company cannot pay debt with paper profits; it needs cold hard cash. So we always check how much of that EBIT is translated into free cash flow. During the last three years, Automatic Data Processing produced sturdy free cash flow equating to 74% of its EBIT, about what we'd expect. This free cash flow puts the company in a good position to pay down debt, when appropriate.Our ViewAutomatic Data Processing's interest cover suggests it can handle its debt as easily as Cristiano Ronaldo could score a goal against an under 14's goalkeeper. And the good news does not stop there, as its net debt to EBITDA also supports that impression! Looking at the bigger picture, we think Automatic Data Processing's use of debt seems quite reasonable and we're not concerned about it. After all, sensible leverage can boost returns on equity. Over time, share prices tend to follow earnings per share, so if you're interested in Automatic Data Processing, you may well want to click here to check an interactive graph of its earnings per share history.Of course, if you're the type of investor who prefers buying stocks without the burden of debt, then don't hesitate to discover our exclusive list of net cash growth stocks, today.Have feedback on this article? column4: Automatic Data Processing (NASDAQ:ADP) Has A Pretty Healthy Balance Sheet
column10: [The external fund manager backed by Berkshire Hathaway's Charlie Munger, Li Lu, makes no bones about it when he says 'The biggest investment risk is not the volatility of prices, but whether you will suffer a permanent loss of capital.' So it seems the smart money knows that debt - which is usually involved in bankruptcies - is a very important factor, when you assess how risky a company is. As with many other companies Automatic Data Processing, Inc. (NASDAQ:ADP) makes use of debt. But the more important question is: how much risk is that debt creating?When Is Debt Dangerous?Debt and other liabilities become risky for a business when it cannot easily fulfill those obligations, either with free cash flow or by raising capital at an attractive price. If things get really bad, the lenders can take control of the business. However, a more common (but still painful) scenario is that it has to raise new equity capital at a low price, thus permanently diluting shareholders. Of course, the upside of debt is that it often represents cheap capital, especially when it replaces dilution in a company with the ability to reinvest at high rates of return. When we think about a company's use of debt, we first look at cash and debt together. See our latest analysis for Automatic Data Processing What Is Automatic Data Processing's Debt?As you can see below, Automatic Data Processing had US$3.10b of debt, at June 2023, which is about the same as the year before. You can click the chart for greater detail. However, it also had US$2.10b in cash, and so its net debt is US$997.4m.debt-equity-history-analysisA Look At Automatic Data Processing's LiabilitiesThe latest balance sheet data shows that Automatic Data Processing had liabilities of US$42.8b due within a year, and liabilities of US$4.69b falling due after that. On the other hand, it had cash of US$2.10b and US$3.01b worth of receivables due within a year. So its liabilities total US$42.4b more than the combination of its cash and short-term receivables.Story continuesWhile this might seem like a lot, it is not so bad since Automatic Data Processing has a huge market capitalization of US$102.3b, and so it could probably strengthen its balance sheet by raising capital if it needed to. But we definitely want to keep our eyes open to indications that its debt is bringing too much risk. Carrying virtually no net debt, Automatic Data Processing has a very light debt load indeed.We use two main ratios to inform us about debt levels relative to earnings. The first is net debt divided by earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA), while the second is how many times its earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) covers its interest expense (or its interest cover, for short). This way, we consider both the absolute quantum of the debt, as well as the interest rates paid on it.Automatic Data Processing's net debt is only 0.20 times its EBITDA. And its EBIT covers its interest expense a whopping 43.9 times over. So you could argue it is no more threatened by its debt than an elephant is by a mouse. Also good is that Automatic Data Processing grew its EBIT at 19% over the last year, further increasing its ability to manage debt. The balance sheet is clearly the area to focus on when you are analysing debt. But ultimately the future profitability of the business will decide if Automatic Data Processing can strengthen its balance sheet over time. So if you want to see what the professionals think, you might find this free report on analyst profit forecasts to be interesting.But our final consideration is also important, because a company cannot pay debt with paper profits; it needs cold hard cash. So we always check how much of that EBIT is translated into free cash flow. During the last three years, Automatic Data Processing produced sturdy free cash flow equating to 74% of its EBIT, about what we'd expect. This free cash flow puts the company in a good position to pay down debt, when appropriate.Our ViewAutomatic Data Processing's interest cover suggests it can handle its debt as easily as Cristiano Ronaldo could score a goal against an under 14's goalkeeper. And the good news does not stop there, as its net debt to EBITDA also supports that impression! Looking at the bigger picture, we think Automatic Data Processing's use of debt seems quite reasonable and we're not concerned about it. After all, sensible leverage can boost returns on equity. Over time, share prices tend to follow earnings per share, so if you're interested in Automatic Data Processing, you may well want to click here to check an interactive graph of its earnings per share history.Of course, if you're the type of investor who prefers buying stocks without the burden of debt, then don't hesitate to discover our exclusive list of net cash growth stocks, today.Have feedback on this article? column10: [Key InsightsInstitutions' substantial holdings in Automatic Data Processing implies that they have significant influence over the company's share priceThe top 25 shareholders own 47% of the company Analyst forecasts along with ownership data serve to give a strong idea about prospects for a businessA look at the shareholders of Automatic Data Processing, Inc. (NASDAQ:ADP) can tell us which group is most powerful. The group holding the most number of shares in the company, around 82% to be precise, is institutions. We would expect most companies to have some institutions on the register, especially if they are growing.As you can see, institutional investors have a fair amount of stake in Automatic Data Processing. This suggests some credibility amongst professional investors. But we can't rely on that fact alone since institutions make bad investments sometimes, just like everyone does. If multiple institutions change their view on a stock at the same time, you could see the share price drop fast. It's therefore worth looking at Automatic Data Processing's earnings history below. Of course, the future is what really matters.earnings-and-revenue-growthInvestors should note that institutions actually own more than half the company, so they can collectively wield significant power. column10: [This article will explore the 20 best Citizenship by Investment programs in 2023. You can skip our comprehensive analysis and proceed directly to the 5 Best Citizenship by Investment Programs in 2023.Over the past decade, individuals with net worth ranging from $2 million to over $50 million have progressively gravitated towards Citizenship by Investment (CBI) programs. Motivated by aspirations for improved mobility, advantageous tax arrangements, and an elevated lifestyle encompassing better education and expanded civil liberties, these programs have surged in popularity.By introducing CBI programs, several smaller countries have strengthened their financial independence and improved their sovereign equity, thereby reducing public debt and reliance on debt financing from supranational organizations.The Allure of Investment Immigration: Embracing Global ProspectsThis rise in interest towards acquiring second citizenship or an alternate nationality holds particular allure for entrepreneurs, especially those classified as High-Net-Worth Individuals (HNWIs). Such a venture opens the gateway to previously untapped business prospects, providing access to emerging markets and highly lucrative opportunities. By exploring these thriving industries and fostering global connections, entrepreneurs can substantially bolster the resilience and prosperity of their ventures.As reported by Investment Migration Council, in 2020, a historical high of 6,705 Americans chose to renounce their citizenship, but this figure notably decreased to 2,426 in 2022. The decline in numbers might partially be attributed to the closure of U.S. embassies during the pandemic. According to a survey conducted by Greenback Expat Tax Services, which polled U.S. expatriates residing in 121 countries, approximately 1 out of every 4 American expatriates is contemplating or actively planning to relinquish their U.S. citizenship. Critics of American tax legislation argue that the country's global income tax compliance and disclosure regulations are excessively burdensome and restrictive.Story continuesWith investors increasingly recognizing the value and potential benefits of a diversified passport portfolio, governments of countries offering investment migration programs also acknowledge the significance of customized immigration policies in attracting investors.On August 15, Bloomberg reported that the European countries offering golden visas have collectively attracted approximately €25 billion (equivalent to $27.1 billion) in foreign direct investment through these schemes over the last ten years. Portugal has stood out as a significant recipient, securing around €6.8 billion (equivalent to $7.3 billion) during this period.HNWI's Preferred Destinations: Tax HavensMany countries with CBI programs provide tax-friendly environments, featuring low or zero-tax regimes for foreign-sourced income, capital gains, and other financial gains. HNWIs can leverage these tax advantages to optimize their global tax position, reducing their tax liabilities significantly. Moreover, some countries grant tax exemptions or reduced personal income tax rates to their new citizens, providing substantial tax savings.Additionally, becoming a citizen of a tax-efficient country can lead to exemptions from wealth and inheritance taxes, preserving family wealth for future generations. Individuals can avoid double taxation and create a financially advantageous global lifestyle by strategically utilizing dual citizenship and tax treaties between nations.Given the substantial wealth and strategic business relocations undertaken by HNWIs and entrepreneurs via CBI programs, several companies specialize in providing bespoke solutions and navigating tax intricacies. QuickBooks Money builds upon QuickBooks' previous financial technology innovations, delivering robust payment and money management features to small businesses through a simplified mobile and web-enabled experience, all without requiring a subscription.Automatic Data Processing (NASDAQ:ADP) provides human resources management and payroll services, including tax-related services.  Automatic Data Processing (NASDAQ:ADP) simplifies HR, payroll, and taxes, benefiting enterprises and HNWIs. On August 3, Automatic Data Processing (NASDAQ:ADP) successfully acquired Honu HR, Inc., doing business as Sora (Sora). Sora is a low-code intelligent workflow automation and data integration solution designed to streamline various business applications, including HR and IT systems, to deliver a more efficient and user-friendly experience for employees, business owners, and HR professionals.Broadridge Financial Solutions, Inc. (NYSE:BR) offers investor communication and technology-driven solutions for financial services firms, including tax reporting services.  Leveraging its communication technology expertise, Broadridge Financial Solutions, Inc. (NYSE:BR) offers crucial tax reporting services for financial firms, HNWIs, and entrepreneurs. On September 14, Broadridge Financial Solutions, Inc. (NYSE: BR) unveiled BRx Match, an all-encompassing cloud-based reconciliation and matching solution. BRx Match has been created to serve as a comprehensive reconciliation platform, capable of addressing both intricate and straightforward reconciliation tasks, thereby empowering business users with the capabilities of an enterprise-level reconciliation solution. This platform streamlines the entire reconciliation process, starting from its earliest stages, leading to enhanced efficiency, transparency, and accuracy, all while mitigating risks and reducing the total cost of ownership.Now that we have taken a look at some major companies that are providing tax and related services for entrepreneurs and high net worth individuals, let's take a look at some of the best Citizenship by Investment programs in 2023.20 Best Citizenship by Investment Programs in 2023Copyright: sidelnikov / 123RF Stock PhotoMethodologyWe determined the 20 best Citizenship by Investment programs in 2023 by evaluating several pivotal criteria of each country: affordability ranking that we gathered from our article (the information provided pertained to the top 15 programs, and we conducted separate research for the remaining 5 programs), tax advantages, political stability, government effectiveness index, and human development insight values.We analyzed data from Trading Economics and KPMG to assess tax friendliness, factoring in personal income tax percentages. Vanuatu and Cape Verde were not included in these lists, so we conducted independent research. The country with the lowest tax rate was assigned the highest rank.In a similar vein, political stability and government effectiveness rankings were informed by The World Bank index, while human development values drew from the United Nations Development Program index. This data was instrumental in crafting our distinct ranking score against each metric.Subsequently, we determined the best Citizenship by Investment programs in 2023 by averaging their placements on these indexes, with a lower average score signifying a more favorable ranking.Please Note:Cape Verde utilizes a progressive personal income tax structure, ranging from 16.5% to 27.5%. We ranked it by calculating its average rate.In cases where multiple countries had similar average scores, their ranking was determined by their tax friendliness score as a decisive factor.We consulted various sources such as Premier Consultancy Group, Global Citizen Solution, IMI Daily, Nomad Capitalist, Immigrant Invest, and Best Citizenships to ascertain investment costs.20 Best Citizenship by Investment Programs in 202320. Once the initial due diligence process is completed, applicants can select their preferred investment route, including bank deposits, treasury bonds, stocks, ownership stakes in corporations, or investments in job-generating businesses.17. This donation's primary objective is to enhance the country's infrastructure, overall development, and economic progress within the region.14. column4: Automatic Data Processing (NASDAQ:ADP) Has A Pretty Healthy Balance Sheet
column10: [The external fund manager backed by Berkshire Hathaway's Charlie Munger, Li Lu, makes no bones about it when he says 'The biggest investment risk is not the volatility of prices, but whether you will suffer a permanent loss of capital.' So it seems the smart money knows that debt - which is usually involved in bankruptcies - is a very important factor, when you assess how risky a company is. As with many other companies Automatic Data Processing, Inc. (NASDAQ:ADP) makes use of debt. But the more important question is: how much risk is that debt creating?When Is Debt Dangerous?Debt and other liabilities become risky for a business when it cannot easily fulfill those obligations, either with free cash flow or by raising capital at an attractive price. If things get really bad, the lenders can take control of the business. However, a more common (but still painful) scenario is that it has to raise new equity capital at a low price, thus permanently diluting shareholders. Of course, the upside of debt is that it often represents cheap capital, especially when it replaces dilution in a company with the ability to reinvest at high rates of return. When we think about a company's use of debt, we first look at cash and debt together. See our latest analysis for Automatic Data Processing What Is Automatic Data Processing's Debt?As you can see below, Automatic Data Processing had US$3.10b of debt, at June 2023, which is about the same as the year before. You can click the chart for greater detail. However, it also had US$2.10b in cash, and so its net debt is US$997.4m.debt-equity-history-analysisA Look At Automatic Data Processing's LiabilitiesThe latest balance sheet data shows that Automatic Data Processing had liabilities of US$42.8b due within a year, and liabilities of US$4.69b falling due after that. On the other hand, it had cash of US$2.10b and US$3.01b worth of receivables due within a year. So its liabilities total US$42.4b more than the combination of its cash and short-term receivables.Story continuesWhile this might seem like a lot, it is not so bad since Automatic Data Processing has a huge market capitalization of US$102.3b, and so it could probably strengthen its balance sheet by raising capital if it needed to. But we definitely want to keep our eyes open to indications that its debt is bringing too much risk. Carrying virtually no net debt, Automatic Data Processing has a very light debt load indeed.We use two main ratios to inform us about debt levels relative to earnings. The first is net debt divided by earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA), while the second is how many times its earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) covers its interest expense (or its interest cover, for short). This way, we consider both the absolute quantum of the debt, as well as the interest rates paid on it.Automatic Data Processing's net debt is only 0.20 times its EBITDA. And its EBIT covers its interest expense a whopping 43.9 times over. So you could argue it is no more threatened by its debt than an elephant is by a mouse. Also good is that Automatic Data Processing grew its EBIT at 19% over the last year, further increasing its ability to manage debt. The balance sheet is clearly the area to focus on when you are analysing debt. But ultimately the future profitability of the business will decide if Automatic Data Processing can strengthen its balance sheet over time. So if you want to see what the professionals think, you might find this free report on analyst profit forecasts to be interesting.But our final consideration is also important, because a company cannot pay debt with paper profits; it needs cold hard cash. So we always check how much of that EBIT is translated into free cash flow. During the last three years, Automatic Data Processing produced sturdy free cash flow equating to 74% of its EBIT, about what we'd expect. This free cash flow puts the company in a good position to pay down debt, when appropriate.Our ViewAutomatic Data Processing's interest cover suggests it can handle its debt as easily as Cristiano Ronaldo could score a goal against an under 14's goalkeeper. And the good news does not stop there, as its net debt to EBITDA also supports that impression! Looking at the bigger picture, we think Automatic Data Processing's use of debt seems quite reasonable and we're not concerned about it. After all, sensible leverage can boost returns on equity. Over time, share prices tend to follow earnings per share, so if you're interested in Automatic Data Processing, you may well want to click here to check an interactive graph of its earnings per share history.Of course, if you're the type of investor who prefers buying stocks without the burden of debt, then don't hesitate to discover our exclusive list of net cash growth stocks, today.Have feedback on this article? column4: Automatic Data Processing (NASDAQ:ADP) Has A Pretty Healthy Balance Sheet
column10: [The external fund manager backed by Berkshire Hathaway's Charlie Munger, Li Lu, makes no bones about it when he says 'The biggest investment risk is not the volatility of prices, but whether you will suffer a permanent loss of capital.' So it seems the smart money knows that debt - which is usually involved in bankruptcies - is a very important factor, when you assess how risky a company is. As with many other companies Automatic Data Processing, Inc. (NASDAQ:ADP) makes use of debt. But the more important question is: how much risk is that debt creating?When Is Debt Dangerous?Debt and other liabilities become risky for a business when it cannot easily fulfill those obligations, either with free cash flow or by raising capital at an attractive price. If things get really bad, the lenders can take control of the business. However, a more common (but still painful) scenario is that it has to raise new equity capital at a low price, thus permanently diluting shareholders. Of course, the upside of debt is that it often represents cheap capital, especially when it replaces dilution in a company with the ability to reinvest at high rates of return. When we think about a company's use of debt, we first look at cash and debt together. See our latest analysis for Automatic Data Processing What Is Automatic Data Processing's Debt?As you can see below, Automatic Data Processing had US$3.10b of debt, at June 2023, which is about the same as the year before. You can click the chart for greater detail. However, it also had US$2.10b in cash, and so its net debt is US$997.4m.debt-equity-history-analysisA Look At Automatic Data Processing's LiabilitiesThe latest balance sheet data shows that Automatic Data Processing had liabilities of US$42.8b due within a year, and liabilities of US$4.69b falling due after that. On the other hand, it had cash of US$2.10b and US$3.01b worth of receivables due within a year. So its liabilities total US$42.4b more than the combination of its cash and short-term receivables.Story continuesWhile this might seem like a lot, it is not so bad since Automatic Data Processing has a huge market capitalization of US$102.3b, and so it could probably strengthen its balance sheet by raising capital if it needed to. But we definitely want to keep our eyes open to indications that its debt is bringing too much risk. Carrying virtually no net debt, Automatic Data Processing has a very light debt load indeed.We use two main ratios to inform us about debt levels relative to earnings. The first is net debt divided by earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA), while the second is how many times its earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) covers its interest expense (or its interest cover, for short). This way, we consider both the absolute quantum of the debt, as well as the interest rates paid on it.Automatic Data Processing's net debt is only 0.20 times its EBITDA. And its EBIT covers its interest expense a whopping 43.9 times over. So you could argue it is no more threatened by its debt than an elephant is by a mouse. Also good is that Automatic Data Processing grew its EBIT at 19% over the last year, further increasing its ability to manage debt. The balance sheet is clearly the area to focus on when you are analysing debt. But ultimately the future profitability of the business will decide if Automatic Data Processing can strengthen its balance sheet over time. So if you want to see what the professionals think, you might find this free report on analyst profit forecasts to be interesting.But our final consideration is also important, because a company cannot pay debt with paper profits; it needs cold hard cash. So we always check how much of that EBIT is translated into free cash flow. During the last three years, Automatic Data Processing produced sturdy free cash flow equating to 74% of its EBIT, about what we'd expect. This free cash flow puts the company in a good position to pay down debt, when appropriate.Our ViewAutomatic Data Processing's interest cover suggests it can handle its debt as easily as Cristiano Ronaldo could score a goal against an under 14's goalkeeper. And the good news does not stop there, as its net debt to EBITDA also supports that impression! Looking at the bigger picture, we think Automatic Data Processing's use of debt seems quite reasonable and we're not concerned about it. After all, sensible leverage can boost returns on equity. Over time, share prices tend to follow earnings per share, so if you're interested in Automatic Data Processing, you may well want to click here to check an interactive graph of its earnings per share history.Of course, if you're the type of investor who prefers buying stocks without the burden of debt, then don't hesitate to discover our exclusive list of net cash growth stocks, today.Have feedback on this article? column4: Is There An Opportunity With Automatic Data Processing, Inc.'s (NASDAQ:ADP) 32% Undervaluation?
column10: [Key InsightsUsing the 2 Stage Free Cash Flow to Equity, Automatic Data Processing fair value estimate is US$355Current share price of US$241 suggests Automatic Data Processing is potentially 32% undervalued Analyst price target for ADP is US$258 which is 27% below our fair value estimateToday we'll do a simple run through of a valuation method used to estimate the attractiveness of Automatic Data Processing, Inc. (NASDAQ:ADP) as an investment opportunity by taking the expected future cash flows and discounting them to their present value. The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model is the tool we will apply to do this. Before you think you won't be able to understand it, just read on! It's actually much less complex than you'd imagine.We would caution that there are many ways of valuing a company and, like the DCF, each technique has advantages and disadvantages in certain scenarios. For those who are keen learners of equity analysis, the Simply Wall St analysis model here may be something of interest to you. See our latest analysis for Automatic Data Processing The MethodWe use what is known as a 2-stage model, which simply means we have two different periods of growth rates for the company's cash flows. Generally the first stage is higher growth, and the second stage is a lower growth phase. To start off with, we need to estimate the next ten years of cash flows. Where possible we use analyst estimates, but when these aren't available we extrapolate the previous free cash flow (FCF) from the last estimate or reported value. We assume companies with shrinking free cash flow will slow their rate of shrinkage, and that companies with growing free cash flow will see their growth rate slow, over this period. We do this to reflect that growth tends to slow more in the early years than it does in later years.Generally we assume that a dollar today is more valuable than a dollar in the future, and so the sum of these future cash flows is then discounted to today's value:Story continues10-year free cash flow (FCF) forecast2024202520262027202820292030203120322033 Levered FCF ($, Millions) US$5.76bUS$5.97bUS$6.66bUS$6.49bUS$6.96bUS$7.21bUS$7.44bUS$7.66bUS$7.86bUS$8.06bGrowth Rate Estimate SourceAnalyst x3Analyst x3Analyst x3Analyst x1Analyst x1Est @ 3.65%Est @ 3.20%Est @ 2.88%Est @ 2.66%Est @ 2.51% Present Value ($, Millions) Discounted @ 6.6% US$5.4kUS$5.3kUS$5.5kUS$5.0kUS$5.1kUS$4.9kUS$4.8kUS$4.6kUS$4.4kUS$4.2k("Est" = FCF growth rate estimated by Simply Wall St)Present Value of 10-year Cash Flow (PVCF) = US$49bThe second stage is also known as Terminal Value, this is the business's cash flow after the first stage. The Gordon Growth formula is used to calculate Terminal Value at a future annual growth rate equal to the 5-year average of the 10-year government bond yield of 2.2%. We discount the terminal cash flows to today's value at a cost of equity of 6.6%.Terminal Value (TV)= FCF2033 × (1 + g) ÷ (r – g) = US$8.1b× (1 + 2.2%) ÷ (6.6%– 2.2%) = US$184bPresent Value of Terminal Value (PVTV)= TV / (1 + r)10= US$184b÷ ( 1 + 6.6%)10= US$97bThe total value is the sum of cash flows for the next ten years plus the discounted terminal value, which results in the Total Equity Value, which in this case is US$146b. In the final step we divide the equity value by the number of shares outstanding. Relative to the current share price of US$241, the company appears quite undervalued at a 32% discount to where the stock price trades currently. The assumptions in any calculation have a big impact on the valuation, so it is better to view this as a rough estimate, not precise down to the last cent.dcfImportant AssumptionsThe calculation above is very dependent on two assumptions. The first is the discount rate and the other is the cash flows. You don't have to agree with these inputs, I recommend redoing the calculations yourself and playing with them. The DCF also does not consider the possible cyclicality of an industry, or a company's future capital requirements, so it does not give a full picture of a company's potential performance. Given that we are looking at Automatic Data Processing as potential shareholders, the cost of equity is used as the discount rate, rather than the cost of capital (or weighted average cost of capital, WACC) which accounts for debt. In this calculation we've used 6.6%, which is based on a levered beta of 0.894. Beta is a measure of a stock's volatility, compared to the market as a whole. We get our beta from the industry average beta of globally comparable companies, with an imposed limit between 0.8 and 2.0, which is a reasonable range for a stable business.SWOT Analysis for Automatic Data ProcessingStrengthEarnings growth over the past year exceeded the industry.Debt is not viewed as a risk.Dividends are covered by earnings and cash flows.WeaknessDividend is low compared to the top 25% of dividend payers in the Professional Services market.OpportunityAnnual earnings are forecast to grow for the next 3 years.Good value based on P/E ratio and estimated fair value.ThreatAnnual earnings are forecast to grow slower than the American market.Looking Ahead:Although the valuation of a company is important, it shouldn't be the only metric you look at when researching a company. The DCF model is not a perfect stock valuation tool. Rather it should be seen as a guide to "what assumptions need to be true for this stock to be under/overvalued?" For instance, if the terminal value growth rate is adjusted slightly, it can dramatically alter the overall result. Can we work out why the company is trading at a discount to intrinsic value? column4: Automatic Data Processing (NASDAQ:ADP) Has A Pretty Healthy Balance Sheet
column10: [The external fund manager backed by Berkshire Hathaway's Charlie Munger, Li Lu, makes no bones about it when he says 'The biggest investment risk is not the volatility of prices, but whether you will suffer a permanent loss of capital.' So it seems the smart money knows that debt - which is usually involved in bankruptcies - is a very important factor, when you assess how risky a company is. As with many other companies Automatic Data Processing, Inc. (NASDAQ:ADP) makes use of debt. But the more important question is: how much risk is that debt creating?When Is Debt Dangerous?Debt and other liabilities become risky for a business when it cannot easily fulfill those obligations, either with free cash flow or by raising capital at an attractive price. If things get really bad, the lenders can take control of the business. However, a more common (but still painful) scenario is that it has to raise new equity capital at a low price, thus permanently diluting shareholders. Of course, the upside of debt is that it often represents cheap capital, especially when it replaces dilution in a company with the ability to reinvest at high rates of return. When we think about a company's use of debt, we first look at cash and debt together. See our latest analysis for Automatic Data Processing What Is Automatic Data Processing's Debt?As you can see below, Automatic Data Processing had US$3.10b of debt, at June 2023, which is about the same as the year before. You can click the chart for greater detail. However, it also had US$2.10b in cash, and so its net debt is US$997.4m.debt-equity-history-analysisA Look At Automatic Data Processing's LiabilitiesThe latest balance sheet data shows that Automatic Data Processing had liabilities of US$42.8b due within a year, and liabilities of US$4.69b falling due after that. On the other hand, it had cash of US$2.10b and US$3.01b worth of receivables due within a year. So its liabilities total US$42.4b more than the combination of its cash and short-term receivables.Story continuesWhile this might seem like a lot, it is not so bad since Automatic Data Processing has a huge market capitalization of US$102.3b, and so it could probably strengthen its balance sheet by raising capital if it needed to. But we definitely want to keep our eyes open to indications that its debt is bringing too much risk. Carrying virtually no net debt, Automatic Data Processing has a very light debt load indeed.We use two main ratios to inform us about debt levels relative to earnings. The first is net debt divided by earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA), while the second is how many times its earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) covers its interest expense (or its interest cover, for short). This way, we consider both the absolute quantum of the debt, as well as the interest rates paid on it.Automatic Data Processing's net debt is only 0.20 times its EBITDA. And its EBIT covers its interest expense a whopping 43.9 times over. So you could argue it is no more threatened by its debt than an elephant is by a mouse. Also good is that Automatic Data Processing grew its EBIT at 19% over the last year, further increasing its ability to manage debt. The balance sheet is clearly the area to focus on when you are analysing debt. But ultimately the future profitability of the business will decide if Automatic Data Processing can strengthen its balance sheet over time. So if you want to see what the professionals think, you might find this free report on analyst profit forecasts to be interesting.But our final consideration is also important, because a company cannot pay debt with paper profits; it needs cold hard cash. So we always check how much of that EBIT is translated into free cash flow. During the last three years, Automatic Data Processing produced sturdy free cash flow equating to 74% of its EBIT, about what we'd expect. This free cash flow puts the company in a good position to pay down debt, when appropriate.Our ViewAutomatic Data Processing's interest cover suggests it can handle its debt as easily as Cristiano Ronaldo could score a goal against an under 14's goalkeeper. And the good news does not stop there, as its net debt to EBITDA also supports that impression! Looking at the bigger picture, we think Automatic Data Processing's use of debt seems quite reasonable and we're not concerned about it. After all, sensible leverage can boost returns on equity. Over time, share prices tend to follow earnings per share, so if you're interested in Automatic Data Processing, you may well want to click here to check an interactive graph of its earnings per share history.Of course, if you're the type of investor who prefers buying stocks without the burden of debt, then don't hesitate to discover our exclusive list of net cash growth stocks, today.Have feedback on this article? column10: [Key InsightsUsing the 2 Stage Free Cash Flow to Equity, Automatic Data Processing fair value estimate is US$355Current share price of US$241 suggests Automatic Data Processing is potentially 32% undervalued Analyst price target for ADP is US$258 which is 27% below our fair value estimateToday we'll do a simple run through of a valuation method used to estimate the attractiveness of Automatic Data Processing, Inc. (NASDAQ:ADP) as an investment opportunity by taking the expected future cash flows and discounting them to their present value. The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model is the tool we will apply to do this. Before you think you won't be able to understand it, just read on! It's actually much less complex than you'd imagine.We would caution that there are many ways of valuing a company and, like the DCF, each technique has advantages and disadvantages in certain scenarios. For those who are keen learners of equity analysis, the Simply Wall St analysis model here may be something of interest to you. See our latest analysis for Automatic Data Processing The MethodWe use what is known as a 2-stage model, which simply means we have two different periods of growth rates for the company's cash flows. Generally the first stage is higher growth, and the second stage is a lower growth phase. To start off with, we need to estimate the next ten years of cash flows. Where possible we use analyst estimates, but when these aren't available we extrapolate the previous free cash flow (FCF) from the last estimate or reported value. We assume companies with shrinking free cash flow will slow their rate of shrinkage, and that companies with growing free cash flow will see their growth rate slow, over this period. We do this to reflect that growth tends to slow more in the early years than it does in later years.Generally we assume that a dollar today is more valuable than a dollar in the future, and so the sum of these future cash flows is then discounted to today's value:Story continues10-year free cash flow (FCF) forecast2024202520262027202820292030203120322033 Levered FCF ($, Millions) US$5.76bUS$5.97bUS$6.66bUS$6.49bUS$6.96bUS$7.21bUS$7.44bUS$7.66bUS$7.86bUS$8.06bGrowth Rate Estimate SourceAnalyst x3Analyst x3Analyst x3Analyst x1Analyst x1Est @ 3.65%Est @ 3.20%Est @ 2.88%Est @ 2.66%Est @ 2.51% Present Value ($, Millions) Discounted @ 6.6% US$5.4kUS$5.3kUS$5.5kUS$5.0kUS$5.1kUS$4.9kUS$4.8kUS$4.6kUS$4.4kUS$4.2k("Est" = FCF growth rate estimated by Simply Wall St)Present Value of 10-year Cash Flow (PVCF) = US$49bThe second stage is also known as Terminal Value, this is the business's cash flow after the first stage. The Gordon Growth formula is used to calculate Terminal Value at a future annual growth rate equal to the 5-year average of the 10-year government bond yield of 2.2%. We discount the terminal cash flows to today's value at a cost of equity of 6.6%.Terminal Value (TV)= FCF2033 × (1 + g) ÷ (r – g) = US$8.1b× (1 + 2.2%) ÷ (6.6%– 2.2%) = US$184bPresent Value of Terminal Value (PVTV)= TV / (1 + r)10= US$184b÷ ( 1 + 6.6%)10= US$97bThe total value is the sum of cash flows for the next ten years plus the discounted terminal value, which results in the Total Equity Value, which in this case is US$146b. In the final step we divide the equity value by the number of shares outstanding. Relative to the current share price of US$241, the company appears quite undervalued at a 32% discount to where the stock price trades currently. The assumptions in any calculation have a big impact on the valuation, so it is better to view this as a rough estimate, not precise down to the last cent.dcfImportant AssumptionsThe calculation above is very dependent on two assumptions. The first is the discount rate and the other is the cash flows. You don't have to agree with these inputs, I recommend redoing the calculations yourself and playing with them. The DCF also does not consider the possible cyclicality of an industry, or a company's future capital requirements, so it does not give a full picture of a company's potential performance. Given that we are looking at Automatic Data Processing as potential shareholders, the cost of equity is used as the discount rate, rather than the cost of capital (or weighted average cost of capital, WACC) which accounts for debt. In this calculation we've used 6.6%, which is based on a levered beta of 0.894. Beta is a measure of a stock's volatility, compared to the market as a whole. We get our beta from the industry average beta of globally comparable companies, with an imposed limit between 0.8 and 2.0, which is a reasonable range for a stable business.SWOT Analysis for Automatic Data ProcessingStrengthEarnings growth over the past year exceeded the industry.Debt is not viewed as a risk.Dividends are covered by earnings and cash flows.WeaknessDividend is low compared to the top 25% of dividend payers in the Professional Services market.OpportunityAnnual earnings are forecast to grow for the next 3 years.Good value based on P/E ratio and estimated fair value.ThreatAnnual earnings are forecast to grow slower than the American market.Looking Ahead:Although the valuation of a company is important, it shouldn't be the only metric you look at when researching a company. The DCF model is not a perfect stock valuation tool. Rather it should be seen as a guide to "what assumptions need to be true for this stock to be under/overvalued?" For instance, if the terminal value growth rate is adjusted slightly, it can dramatically alter the overall result. Can we work out why the company is trading at a discount to intrinsic value? If multiple institutions change their view on a stock at the same time, you could see the share price drop fast. It's therefore worth looking at Automatic Data Processing's earnings history below. Such a venture opens the gateway to previously untapped business prospects, providing access to emerging markets and highly lucrative opportunities. By exploring these thriving industries and fostering global connections, entrepreneurs can substantially bolster the resilience and prosperity of their ventures.As reported by Investment Migration Council, in 2020, a historical high of 6,705 Americans chose to renounce their citizenship, but this figure notably decreased to 2,426 in 2022. The decline in numbers might partially be attributed to the closure of U.S. embassies during the pandemic. According to a survey conducted by Greenback Expat Tax Services, which polled U.S. expatriates residing in 121 countries, approximately 1 out of every 4 American expatriates is contemplating or actively planning to relinquish their U.S. citizenship. Critics of American tax legislation argue that the country's global income tax compliance and disclosure regulations are excessively burdensome and restrictive.Story continuesWith investors increasingly recognizing the value and potential benefits of a diversified passport portfolio, governments of countries offering investment migration programs also acknowledge the significance of customized immigration policies in attracting investors.On August 15, Bloomberg reported that the European countries offering golden visas have collectively attracted approximately €25 billion (equivalent to $27.1 billion) in foreign direct investment through these schemes over the last ten years. HNWIs can leverage these tax advantages to optimize their global tax position, reducing their tax liabilities significantly. Moreover, some countries grant tax exemptions or reduced personal income tax rates to their new citizens, providing substantial tax savings.Additionally, becoming a citizen of a tax-efficient country can lead to exemptions from wealth and inheritance taxes, preserving family wealth for future generations. This platform streamlines the entire reconciliation process, starting from its earliest stages, leading to enhanced efficiency, transparency, and accuracy, all while mitigating risks and reducing the total cost of ownership.Now that we have taken a look at some major companies that are providing tax and related services for entrepreneurs and high net worth individuals, let's take a look at some of the best Citizenship by Investment programs in 2023.20 Best Citizenship by Investment Programs in 2023Copyright: sidelnikov / 123RF Stock PhotoMethodologyWe determined the 20 best Citizenship by Investment programs in 2023 by evaluating several pivotal criteria of each country: affordability ranking that we gathered from our article (the information provided pertained to the top 15 programs, and we conducted separate research for the remaining 5 programs), tax advantages, political stability, government effectiveness index, and human development insight values.We analyzed data from Trading Economics and KPMG to assess tax friendliness, factoring in personal income tax percentages. column4: Automatic Data Processing (NASDAQ:ADP) Has A Pretty Healthy Balance Sheet
column10: [The external fund manager backed by Berkshire Hathaway's Charlie Munger, Li Lu, makes no bones about it when he says 'The biggest investment risk is not the volatility of prices, but whether you will suffer a permanent loss of capital.' So it seems the smart money knows that debt - which is usually involved in bankruptcies - is a very important factor, when you assess how risky a company is. As with many other companies Automatic Data Processing, Inc. (NASDAQ:ADP) makes use of debt. But the more important question is: how much risk is that debt creating?When Is Debt Dangerous?Debt and other liabilities become risky for a business when it cannot easily fulfill those obligations, either with free cash flow or by raising capital at an attractive price. If things get really bad, the lenders can take control of the business. However, a more common (but still painful) scenario is that it has to raise new equity capital at a low price, thus permanently diluting shareholders. Of course, the upside of debt is that it often represents cheap capital, especially when it replaces dilution in a company with the ability to reinvest at high rates of return. When we think about a company's use of debt, we first look at cash and debt together. See our latest analysis for Automatic Data Processing What Is Automatic Data Processing's Debt?As you can see below, Automatic Data Processing had US$3.10b of debt, at June 2023, which is about the same as the year before. You can click the chart for greater detail. However, it also had US$2.10b in cash, and so its net debt is US$997.4m.debt-equity-history-analysisA Look At Automatic Data Processing's LiabilitiesThe latest balance sheet data shows that Automatic Data Processing had liabilities of US$42.8b due within a year, and liabilities of US$4.69b falling due after that. On the other hand, it had cash of US$2.10b and US$3.01b worth of receivables due within a year. So its liabilities total US$42.4b more than the combination of its cash and short-term receivables.Story continuesWhile this might seem like a lot, it is not so bad since Automatic Data Processing has a huge market capitalization of US$102.3b, and so it could probably strengthen its balance sheet by raising capital if it needed to. But we definitely want to keep our eyes open to indications that its debt is bringing too much risk. Carrying virtually no net debt, Automatic Data Processing has a very light debt load indeed.We use two main ratios to inform us about debt levels relative to earnings. The first is net debt divided by earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA), while the second is how many times its earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) covers its interest expense (or its interest cover, for short). This way, we consider both the absolute quantum of the debt, as well as the interest rates paid on it.Automatic Data Processing's net debt is only 0.20 times its EBITDA. And its EBIT covers its interest expense a whopping 43.9 times over. So you could argue it is no more threatened by its debt than an elephant is by a mouse. Also good is that Automatic Data Processing grew its EBIT at 19% over the last year, further increasing its ability to manage debt. The balance sheet is clearly the area to focus on when you are analysing debt. But ultimately the future profitability of the business will decide if Automatic Data Processing can strengthen its balance sheet over time. So if you want to see what the professionals think, you might find this free report on analyst profit forecasts to be interesting.But our final consideration is also important, because a company cannot pay debt with paper profits; it needs cold hard cash. So we always check how much of that EBIT is translated into free cash flow. During the last three years, Automatic Data Processing produced sturdy free cash flow equating to 74% of its EBIT, about what we'd expect. This free cash flow puts the company in a good position to pay down debt, when appropriate.Our ViewAutomatic Data Processing's interest cover suggests it can handle its debt as easily as Cristiano Ronaldo could score a goal against an under 14's goalkeeper. And the good news does not stop there, as its net debt to EBITDA also supports that impression! Looking at the bigger picture, we think Automatic Data Processing's use of debt seems quite reasonable and we're not concerned about it. After all, sensible leverage can boost returns on equity. Over time, share prices tend to follow earnings per share, so if you're interested in Automatic Data Processing, you may well want to click here to check an interactive graph of its earnings per share history.Of course, if you're the type of investor who prefers buying stocks without the burden of debt, then don't hesitate to discover our exclusive list of net cash growth stocks, today.Have feedback on this article? column10: [Key InsightsUsing the 2 Stage Free Cash Flow to Equity, Automatic Data Processing fair value estimate is US$355Current share price of US$241 suggests Automatic Data Processing is potentially 32% undervalued Analyst price target for ADP is US$258 which is 27% below our fair value estimateToday we'll do a simple run through of a valuation method used to estimate the attractiveness of Automatic Data Processing, Inc. (NASDAQ:ADP) as an investment opportunity by taking the expected future cash flows and discounting them to their present value. The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model is the tool we will apply to do this. Before you think you won't be able to understand it, just read on! It's actually much less complex than you'd imagine.We would caution that there are many ways of valuing a company and, like the DCF, each technique has advantages and disadvantages in certain scenarios. For those who are keen learners of equity analysis, the Simply Wall St analysis model here may be something of interest to you. See our latest analysis for Automatic Data Processing The MethodWe use what is known as a 2-stage model, which simply means we have two different periods of growth rates for the company's cash flows. Generally the first stage is higher growth, and the second stage is a lower growth phase. To start off with, we need to estimate the next ten years of cash flows. Where possible we use analyst estimates, but when these aren't available we extrapolate the previous free cash flow (FCF) from the last estimate or reported value. We assume companies with shrinking free cash flow will slow their rate of shrinkage, and that companies with growing free cash flow will see their growth rate slow, over this period. We do this to reflect that growth tends to slow more in the early years than it does in later years.Generally we assume that a dollar today is more valuable than a dollar in the future, and so the sum of these future cash flows is then discounted to today's value:Story continues10-year free cash flow (FCF) forecast2024202520262027202820292030203120322033 Levered FCF ($, Millions) US$5.76bUS$5.97bUS$6.66bUS$6.49bUS$6.96bUS$7.21bUS$7.44bUS$7.66bUS$7.86bUS$8.06bGrowth Rate Estimate SourceAnalyst x3Analyst x3Analyst x3Analyst x1Analyst x1Est @ 3.65%Est @ 3.20%Est @ 2.88%Est @ 2.66%Est @ 2.51% Present Value ($, Millions) Discounted @ 6.6% US$5.4kUS$5.3kUS$5.5kUS$5.0kUS$5.1kUS$4.9kUS$4.8kUS$4.6kUS$4.4kUS$4.2k("Est" = FCF growth rate estimated by Simply Wall St)Present Value of 10-year Cash Flow (PVCF) = US$49bThe second stage is also known as Terminal Value, this is the business's cash flow after the first stage. The Gordon Growth formula is used to calculate Terminal Value at a future annual growth rate equal to the 5-year average of the 10-year government bond yield of 2.2%. We discount the terminal cash flows to today's value at a cost of equity of 6.6%.Terminal Value (TV)= FCF2033 × (1 + g) ÷ (r – g) = US$8.1b× (1 + 2.2%) ÷ (6.6%– 2.2%) = US$184bPresent Value of Terminal Value (PVTV)= TV / (1 + r)10= US$184b÷ ( 1 + 6.6%)10= US$97bThe total value is the sum of cash flows for the next ten years plus the discounted terminal value, which results in the Total Equity Value, which in this case is US$146b. In the final step we divide the equity value by the number of shares outstanding. Relative to the current share price of US$241, the company appears quite undervalued at a 32% discount to where the stock price trades currently. The assumptions in any calculation have a big impact on the valuation, so it is better to view this as a rough estimate, not precise down to the last cent.dcfImportant AssumptionsThe calculation above is very dependent on two assumptions. The first is the discount rate and the other is the cash flows. You don't have to agree with these inputs, I recommend redoing the calculations yourself and playing with them. The DCF also does not consider the possible cyclicality of an industry, or a company's future capital requirements, so it does not give a full picture of a company's potential performance. Given that we are looking at Automatic Data Processing as potential shareholders, the cost of equity is used as the discount rate, rather than the cost of capital (or weighted average cost of capital, WACC) which accounts for debt. In this calculation we've used 6.6%, which is based on a levered beta of 0.894. Beta is a measure of a stock's volatility, compared to the market as a whole. We get our beta from the industry average beta of globally comparable companies, with an imposed limit between 0.8 and 2.0, which is a reasonable range for a stable business.SWOT Analysis for Automatic Data ProcessingStrengthEarnings growth over the past year exceeded the industry.Debt is not viewed as a risk.Dividends are covered by earnings and cash flows.WeaknessDividend is low compared to the top 25% of dividend payers in the Professional Services market.OpportunityAnnual earnings are forecast to grow for the next 3 years.Good value based on P/E ratio and estimated fair value.ThreatAnnual earnings are forecast to grow slower than the American market.Looking Ahead:Although the valuation of a company is important, it shouldn't be the only metric you look at when researching a company. The DCF model is not a perfect stock valuation tool. Rather it should be seen as a guide to "what assumptions need to be true for this stock to be under/overvalued?" For instance, if the terminal value growth rate is adjusted slightly, it can dramatically alter the overall result. Can we work out why the company is trading at a discount to intrinsic value? On Sep 26, the Conference Board reported that the index for Consumer Confidence in September came in at 103, missing the consensus estimate of 105.5.The metric for August was revised upward to 108.7 from 106.1 reported earlier. September marked the second consecutive month of the index’s decline and the largest monthly decline for the index since December 2020.The Present Situation Index— based on consumers’ assessment of current business and labor market conditions— rose marginally to 147.1 in September from 146.7 in August. The Expectations Index— based on consumers’ short-term outlook for income, business, and labor market conditions— declined to 73.7 in September, after falling to 83.3 in August and 88 in July. Notably, any reading of the Expectations Index below 80, historically signals a recession within next year.According to Dana Peterson, the chief economist at The Conference Board, “Expectations for the next six months tumbled back below the recession threshold of 80, reflecting less confidence about future business conditions, job availability, and incomes."Peterson also said, "Consumers may be hearing more bad news about corporate earnings, while job openings are narrowing, and interest rates continue to rise — making big-ticket items more expensive."In a similar kind of study, on Sep 15, the University of Michigan reported that the preliminary Index for U.S. Consumer Sentiment in September dropped to 67.7, missing the consensus estimate of 69.2. column4: With 6.5% one-year returns, institutional owners may ignore Automatic Data Processing, Inc.'s (NASDAQ:ADP) 3.5% stock price decline
column10: [Key InsightsInstitutions' substantial holdings in Automatic Data Processing implies that they have significant influence over the company's share priceThe top 25 shareholders own 47% of the company Analyst forecasts along with ownership data serve to give a strong idea about prospects for a businessA look at the shareholders of Automatic Data Processing, Inc. (NASDAQ:ADP) can tell us which group is most powerful. The group holding the most number of shares in the company, around 82% to be precise, is institutions. Put another way, the group faces the maximum upside potential (or downside risk).Institutional investors was the group most impacted after the company's market cap fell to US$98b last week. However, the 6.5% one-year return to shareholders may have helped lessen their pain. We would assume however, that they would be on the lookout for weakness in the future.In the chart below, we zoom in on the different ownership groups of Automatic Data Processing. View our latest analysis for Automatic Data Processing ownership-breakdownWhat Does The Institutional Ownership Tell Us About Automatic Data Processing?Institutions typically measure themselves against a benchmark when reporting to their own investors, so they often become more enthusiastic about a stock once it's included in a major index. We would expect most companies to have some institutions on the register, especially if they are growing.As you can see, institutional investors have a fair amount of stake in Automatic Data Processing. This suggests some credibility amongst professional investors. But we can't rely on that fact alone since institutions make bad investments sometimes, just like everyone does. If multiple institutions change their view on a stock at the same time, you could see the share price drop fast. It's therefore worth looking at Automatic Data Processing's earnings history below. Of course, the future is what really matters.earnings-and-revenue-growthInvestors should note that institutions actually own more than half the company, so they can collectively wield significant power. Automatic Data Processing is not owned by hedge funds. The Vanguard Group, Inc. is currently the largest shareholder, with 9.5% of shares outstanding. Meanwhile, the second and third largest shareholders, hold 8.2% and 4.4%, of the shares outstanding, respectively.Story continuesOn studying our ownership data, we found that 25 of the top shareholders collectively own less than 50% of the share register, implying that no single individual has a majority interest.Researching institutional ownership is a good way to gauge and filter a stock's expected performance. The same can be achieved by studying analyst sentiments. Quite a few analysts cover the stock, so you could look into forecast growth quite easily.Insider Ownership Of Automatic Data ProcessingThe definition of company insiders can be subjective and does vary between jurisdictions. Our data reflects individual insiders, capturing board members at the very least. Company management run the business, but the CEO will answer to the board, even if he or she is a member of it.Most consider insider ownership a positive because it can indicate the board is well aligned with other shareholders. However, on some occasions too much power is concentrated within this group.Our data suggests that insiders own under 1% of Automatic Data Processing, Inc. in their own names. It is a very large company, so it would be surprising to see insiders own a large proportion of the company. Though their holding amounts to less than 1%, we can see that board members collectively own US$87m worth of shares (at current prices). Arguably recent buying and selling is just as important to consider. You can  click here to see if insiders have been buying or selling. General Public OwnershipThe general public, who are usually individual investors, hold a 18% stake in Automatic Data Processing. This size of ownership, while considerable, may not be enough to change company policy if the decision is not in sync with other large shareholders.Next Steps:It's always worth thinking about the different groups who own shares in a company. But to understand Automatic Data Processing better, we need to consider many other factors.I always like to check for a history of revenue growth. You can too, by accessing this free chart of historic revenue and earnings in this detailed graph.Ultimately the future is most important. You can access this free report on analyst forecasts for the company.NB: Figures in this article are calculated using data from the last twelve months, which refer to the 12-month period ending on the last date of the month the financial statement is dated. This may not be consistent with full year annual report figures.Have feedback on this article? Concerned about the content? Get in touch with us directly. column4: 20 Best Citizenship by Investment Programs in 2023
column10: [This article will explore the 20 best Citizenship by Investment programs in 2023. You can skip our comprehensive analysis and proceed directly to the 5 Best Citizenship by Investment Programs in 2023.Over the past decade, individuals with net worth ranging from $2 million to over $50 million have progressively gravitated towards Citizenship by Investment (CBI) programs. Motivated by aspirations for improved mobility, advantageous tax arrangements, and an elevated lifestyle encompassing better education and expanded civil liberties, these programs have surged in popularity.By introducing CBI programs, several smaller countries have strengthened their financial independence and improved their sovereign equity, thereby reducing public debt and reliance on debt financing from supranational organizations.The Allure of Investment Immigration: Embracing Global ProspectsThis rise in interest towards acquiring second citizenship or an alternate nationality holds particular allure for entrepreneurs, especially those classified as High-Net-Worth Individuals (HNWIs). Such a venture opens the gateway to previously untapped business prospects, providing access to emerging markets and highly lucrative opportunities. By exploring these thriving industries and fostering global connections, entrepreneurs can substantially bolster the resilience and prosperity of their ventures.As reported by Investment Migration Council, in 2020, a historical high of 6,705 Americans chose to renounce their citizenship, but this figure notably decreased to 2,426 in 2022. The decline in numbers might partially be attributed to the closure of U.S. embassies during the pandemic. According to a survey conducted by Greenback Expat Tax Services, which polled U.S. expatriates residing in 121 countries, approximately 1 out of every 4 American expatriates is contemplating or actively planning to relinquish their U.S. citizenship. Critics of American tax legislation argue that the country's global income tax compliance and disclosure regulations are excessively burdensome and restrictive.Story continuesWith investors increasingly recognizing the value and potential benefits of a diversified passport portfolio, governments of countries offering investment migration programs also acknowledge the significance of customized immigration policies in attracting investors.On August 15, Bloomberg reported that the European countries offering golden visas have collectively attracted approximately €25 billion (equivalent to $27.1 billion) in foreign direct investment through these schemes over the last ten years. Portugal has stood out as a significant recipient, securing around €6.8 billion (equivalent to $7.3 billion) during this period.HNWI's Preferred Destinations: Tax HavensMany countries with CBI programs provide tax-friendly environments, featuring low or zero-tax regimes for foreign-sourced income, capital gains, and other financial gains. HNWIs can leverage these tax advantages to optimize their global tax position, reducing their tax liabilities significantly. Moreover, some countries grant tax exemptions or reduced personal income tax rates to their new citizens, providing substantial tax savings.Additionally, becoming a citizen of a tax-efficient country can lead to exemptions from wealth and inheritance taxes, preserving family wealth for future generations. Individuals can avoid double taxation and create a financially advantageous global lifestyle by strategically utilizing dual citizenship and tax treaties between nations.Given the substantial wealth and strategic business relocations undertaken by HNWIs and entrepreneurs via CBI programs, several companies specialize in providing bespoke solutions and navigating tax intricacies. Distinguished companies acclaimed for their services include Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU), Automatic Data Processing (NASDAQ:ADP), and Broadridge Financial Solutions, Inc. (NYSE:BR).Intuit Inc.
